name: early_deterioration
title: Early deterioration
outcome: Deterioration (a vital-sign danger rule sustained for 30 minutes) within the next 6 hours
label: Deterioration in the next 6 hours

metrics.reported_on: The author's own test split of a 300-patient, 7,200-row file that is not in the hand-over
metrics.note: Checked on the platform. Scored with the model's own columns on the shared training data it ranks patients no better than chance (AUROC 0.51; 0.64 on the MIMIC rows). Through the platform's feature builder, which fills the gaps it never saw in training, AUROC is 0.75 on the MIMIC snapshots (23 events in 315): weak, and two thirds of snapshots would sit above the author's lower (0.009) threshold, which the platform therefore does not use.

trained_on: A 300-patient, 7,200-row version of the training data (rpm_training_sample_test.csv), not the shared file
limitations: On the shared training data the model performs at chance level, so it is not validated: on its own it cannot page anyone or start agent work. It never saw a missing value in training, while the platform cannot supply activity, steps or patient-reported scores live: those are carried forward from the last recorded snapshot and other gaps are filled with training medians. Trained on post-discharge snapshots, so it runs for patients at home only; ICU patients rely on the NEWS2 rules. For a patient without a hospital record, age comes from the registration and the record's labs and charted vital signs are set to the training medians: the result is marked as estimated. The author's 'red' threshold (90% recall, 0.009) is lower than the 'yellow' one (70% recall, 0.272); the platform alerts from the 0.272 threshold only; below it the result is shown as low. For a patient at home, a medium NEWS2 or vital-sign finding becomes an alert only when this model (or the other confirming model) is at or above its alert threshold.
source: Early deterioration model/deployment/artifacts (hand-over of 2026-10-14); the 3-hour model is not served
